runset_question: What is the minimum slow negative control?
current_answer: A nearby callback, delayed task, worker lifetime, IPC shape, or idle child is not sufficient.
minimum_rows: near-key marker no-op, delayed no-op, worker delay with no message, external delay with no message, and idle child plus no-op.
current_local_result: Near-key no-CPU task controls have median p50 24.3ms and min-max 22.2-24.6ms.
required_counters: Confirm no helper CPU work; align helper lifetime, timer fire, next keydown enqueue, EventDispatch start/end, renderer wakeups, process QoS, core ID, frequency, and residency.
acceptance_or_rejection_rule: Rows must stay slow while fast CPU rows show a counter delta; if they become fast with the same counters, the CPU-state explanation is too narrow.

runset_question: What is the minimum fast continuous control?
current_answer: Ordinary or utility-QoS CPU activity is sufficient locally.
minimum_rows: ordinary external CPU, nice +20 CPU, taskpolicy -c utility CPU, and one representative taskpolicy -l/-t tier row.
current_local_result: Continuous ordinary/utility controls have median p50 9.7ms; taskpolicy -c utility is 9.4ms; taskpolicy -l/-t tiers are 9.2-9.7ms.
required_counters: Capture helper effective QoS, helper CPU consumption, renderer runnable-to-running latency, renderer core ID, performance-cluster residency, frequency, package power, and EventDispatch source spans.
discriminates: P-core/frequency/residency, ordinary/utility scheduler visibility, and foreground renderer scheduling improvements.
acceptance_or_rejection_rule: Fast rows should share a measurable OS or browser-scheduler state not present in slow no-CPU and background/maintenance rows; otherwise this boundary remains descriptive only.

runset_question: What is the minimum slow continuous policy contrast?
current_answer: CPU consumption alone is not enough when the helper is background or maintenance clamped.
minimum_rows: taskpolicy -b CPU x1/x4/x8, taskpolicy -c background CPU, and taskpolicy -c maintenance CPU.
current_local_result: Continuous background/maintenance controls have median p50 24.2ms and min-max 24.0-24.7ms despite real CPU consumption.
required_counters: Verify helper CPU consumption and effective QoS; capture renderer scheduling latency, helper/renderer core placement, performance-cluster residency, frequency, package power, and browser input-task priority.
discriminates: Generic CPU load versus policy-visible CPU state.
acceptance_or_rejection_rule: If background/maintenance rows consume CPU but lack the fast rows' residency, frequency, scheduler, or browser-task state, the policy-sensitive mechanism is supported; if counters match fast rows while latency stays slow, look at browser or cache state.

runset_question: How should finite CPU duration and recency be tested?
current_answer: The finite-burst controls show a descriptive duration/proximity relationship, but not the lower-level cause.
minimum_rows: 20ms, 40ms, 80ms, and 150ms worker/external/prestarted CPU rows near keydown, plus 150ms rows at earlier end-to-keydown gaps.
current_local_result: The two-term finite-burst model has R^2 0.71; longer work lowers p50 and larger end-to-keydown gaps raise p50.
required_counters: Record helper work start/end, work duration, work-end-to-keydown gap, per-core residency/frequency decay, renderer scheduling latency, cache/memory counters if available, and EventDispatch subspans.
discriminates: Power/frequency decay, scheduler-state decay, cache warmth, or timer/wakeup latency.
acceptance_or_rejection_rule: A valid mechanism must explain both the continuous QoS split and the finite-burst decay; explaining only the decay is not enough to close the CPU/QoS question.

runset_question: How should OS counters be separated from Chromium scheduler state?
current_answer: Current Chromium traces do not contain the scheduler/runtime state needed to split OS from browser mechanisms.
minimum_rows: Run the no-CPU slow row, one ordinary/utility fast row, one background/maintenance slow row, one finite-burst fast row, and one stale finite-burst slow row with matching Chromium scheduler/runtime traces.
current_local_result: Browser/runtime checkpoints and CPU/QoS controls both show state below Gutenberg selectors, but current visual traces are render/screenshot oriented.
required_counters: Add Chromium scheduler/task-queue categories, renderer main-thread task boundaries, input task priority, V8 slices, protocol markers, and existing Gutenberg source spans to the same key windows as the OS counters.
discriminates: OS power/scheduler state versus Chromium input-task scheduling state.
acceptance_or_rejection_rule: Claim a browser-scheduler mechanism only if OS frequency/residency/QoS counters do not explain the split and Chromium queue/priority/task boundaries do; otherwise keep the mechanism at the OS-counter layer.

runset_question: What report shape is required before changing the mechanism claim?
current_answer: Aggregate p50 rows are not enough for the remaining mechanism layer.
minimum_rows: All rows above, with per-sample records rather than only class medians.
current_local_result: Existing summaries identify the boundary classes but not the lower-level state.
required_counters: For each sample, report run id, sample index, retained/throwaway status, key timing, EventDispatch timing, helper work timing, helper QoS, renderer QoS, core IDs, frequency/residency, power/thermal metadata, browser scheduler slices, source-span ids, and environment metadata.
discriminates: Per-sample causal alignment versus aggregate coincidence.
acceptance_or_rejection_rule: Do not revise the CPU/QoS mechanism claim unless the same per-sample counter state predicts the fast/slow split across slow no-CPU, fast ordinary/utility, slow background/maintenance, and finite decay rows.
